title: Doodle generative compositions in your browser with Musical Spirograph
summary: Musical Spirograph is a browser-based tool that combines generative music composition with mathematical spirograph patterns. Points moving according to equations generate hypotrochoids and epitrochoids that pass through concentric rings to trigger musical notes. The tool offers customization with six virtual rotors and multiple drawing arms.
content:
So pretty. | Screenshot: Terrence O’Brien / The Verge	

I remember having a Spirograph as a kid and being obsessed with it. Its geometric patterns are hypnotic and gorgeous. I also love generative music composition. So bringing those two things together in a browser tab, I'm hooked. Musical Spirograph is a relatively simple concept. A set of points dash around the screen according to mathematical equations, generating hypotrochoids and epitrochoids. Those points pass through a series of concentric rings which trigger specific notes.
Honestly, that alone is fun enough, but you can customize it quite a bit. There are six different virtual rotors to pick from, you can have up to three arms drawing  …

title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
summary: OpenAI is reversing its previous opposition to California's SB 53 AI safety bill, now calling for it to be strengthened. The move reflects a shift in the company's regulatory stance on state-level AI safety measures.
content: OpenAI is calling for California to strengthen SB 53, an AI safety bill that the company previously opposed.

title: Frontier AI labs still won’t say how they’d contain a rogue model
summary: A new study reveals that leading AI labs lack publicly documented plans for containing rogue models, despite the potential risks as AI systems become more sophisticated. The findings raise concerns about industry preparedness for controlling autonomous AI systems that could behave unexpectedly.
content: A new study finds leading AI labs have few publicly documented plans for containing rogue models, raising questions about preparedness as AI systems increasingly demonstrate unexpected and potentially dangerous behavior.

title: US battery startups have found a lifeline in defense
summary: U.S. battery startups have secured $500 million in grants from the Department of Energy, providing critical support to an industry struggling after EV incentive cuts. The defense-backed funding offers a new survival pathway for companies facing market challenges.
content: U.S. battery startups pulled in $500 million in grants from the Department of Energy, throwing a lifeline to an industry that was on the ropes after EV incentives were slashed.

title: Pixel 11 Pro XL review: Snappier cameras can’t hide an iterative upgrade
summary: Google's Pixel 11 Pro XL features improved cameras and AI capabilities like Rambler, but the upgrades are largely incremental. The review questions whether the improvements justify an upgrade for existing Pixel owners.
content: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro XL brings snappier cameras and genuinely useful AI features like Rambler, but its iterative upgrades may not be enough to tempt recent Pixel owners.

title: Amazon just hiked the prices for Echo, Fire TV, and Kindle products by up to 60 percent
summary: Amazon has raised prices across its device lineup by up to 60 percent, citing increased memory and storage component costs. Budget-friendly products were hit hardest, with the Echo Dot jumping 60 percent from $49.99 to $79.99, and the base Kindle rising 37 percent to $149.99.
content:
The Echo Dot Max went from $99.99 to $119.99 overnight, while its sibling the Echo Dot jumped to $79.99 from $49.99. | Photo by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge	

Citing "significant increases in memory and storage component costs," Amazon has raised prices on Echos, Kindles, Fire TVs, and Eeros by up to 60 percent, as first reported by Fortune.
The cheapest products in Amazon's lineup were hit hardest, with the Echo Dot smart speaker jumping from $49.99 to $79.99. The Fire TV Stick 4K Max also rose by over 40 percent to $84.99, and the base level Kindle now costs $149.99, a nearly 37 percent increase.

title: An okay laptop with 16GB of RAM is better than a nice laptop with 8GB, and this $520 HP OmniBook proves it
summary: HP's OmniBook 3 challenges the trend of underpowered budget laptops by offering 16GB of RAM at a $520 price point. The review argues that adequate RAM matters more than build quality on tight budgets, as memory constraints have become a significant bottleneck in low-cost laptops.
content:
The OmniBook 3 isn’t a sweet treat, but it gets things done on the cheap. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge	

Laptop prices are out of whack. $500 used to get you a tolerable laptop, and $900 got you a really good one. They often had similar CPU, RAM, and storage options because that stuff was comparatively cheap; the difference was often in build quality and screen rather than power. But RAMageddon has thrown everything off. Even laptops like the $950 Surface Laptop now start with 8GB of RAM, which isn't enough. And on the lower end, where manufacturers are struggling to compete with the $700 MacBook Neo, they're cutting corners on storage, CPU, and build quality too.
However, one low-cost laptop has bucked this and genuinely surprised me. HP's 16 …

title: Putting mice into hibernation causes a major loss of synapses
summary: Research on hibernating mice reveals that the brain dramatically reduces the number of synapses during hibernation, yet mice retain their memories despite this loss. The finding suggests memory formation may rely on mechanisms beyond synapse density.
content: Hibernation cuts down on synapses, but mice seem to retain memories anyway.

zh.title: 让老鼠冬眠导致大量突触丧失
zh.summary: 对冬眠老鼠的研究表明，在冬眠期间大脑会大幅减少突触数量，但老鼠尽管这种损失仍保留了记忆。该发现表明记忆形成可能依赖于超越突触密度的机制。

title: Dismantling the Roadless Rule threatens to disrupt wildlife and water in US
summary: The Trump administration's proposed rollback of the Roadless Rule would open protected federal lands to road construction, threatening wildlife habitats and freshwater resources. The change marks a significant shift in U.S. conservation policy.
content: Lands free of roads are under threat from the Trump administration’s proposed rollback.

zh.title: 废除无路规则威胁破坏美国的野生动物和水资源
zh.summary: 特朗普政府拟议的无路规则撤销将使受保护的联邦土地开放用于道路建设，威胁野生动物栖息地和淡水资源。这一变化标志着美国保护政策的重大转变。

title: Michael Polansky is training an AI model on skin that’s still alive
summary: Michael Polansky, known as Lady Gaga's partner and former Sean Parker deputy, has founded an AI startup that maintains living human skin tissue outside the body for weeks to identify new skincare compounds. The company is going public after years of development, representing a novel approach to cosmetic research.
content: Michael Polansky — better known publicly as Lady Gaga's partner and a former top deputy to Sean Parker — has quietly spent years building an AI-driven startup that keeps living human skin tissue alive for weeks outside the body to discover new skincare compounds, and is only now going public about it.

title: Japanese space tech startup Letara expands beyond satellite thrusters with $16M
summary: Letara, a Japanese space startup, is expanding from satellite propulsion into broader space, defense, and security markets after securing $16 million in funding for its hybrid rocket technology.
content: Japanese space startup Letara is betting its hybrid rocket technology can move beyond small satellite thrusters into a broader market for space, defense and security, after raising ¥2.6 billion ($16 million).
